elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 states that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the law of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 expressly grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 expressly grants exclusive jurisdiction to the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The governing law is the law of one accepted fallback jurisdiction: Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales law.

elements.element: The clause designates the corresponding accepted fallback courts: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause designates New York County state and federal courts rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or London courts.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred New York law and exclusive New York County state-and-federal-court position. Replacing the Singapore governing-law provision, removing the conflicting Singapore forum, and confining injunctive relief to the selected New York courts are necessary to make the forum exclusive. The remaining submission and waiver provisions are preserved without contradiction.
